outputs.agentty --help:
agentty 0.9.51

usage: agentty [subcommand] [options]

subcommands
  login             Authenticate (API key, or OAuth via claude.ai)
  logout            Remove saved credentials
  status            Show current auth status
  airgap            Launch agentty on an air-gapped host via SSH tunnel
                    (`agentty airgap --help` for details)
  acp               Run as an ACP agent over stdio (for Zed et al.)
  paste [cmd]       Clipboard tools (richpaste). `paste setup` once on your
                    laptop makes Ctrl+V images work over ssh; `paste` prints the
                    clipboard, `paste doctor` explains the route, `paste config`
                    lists and sets the paste settings, `paste help` lists the
                    rest
  run [PROMPT]      Headless one-shot: run PROMPT through the full agent loop
                    (tools, sandbox) and print only the answer to stdout. PROMPT
                    `-` or absent reads stdin: `git diff | agentty run "review
                    this"`. Flags: --agent TYPE (general, explorer, reviewer,
                    tester, coder), --json, -o FILE, --max-turns N, --timeout
                    5m, --effort LEVEL, --read-only, --no-network, --save, --
                    resume ID|last, --events jsonl (tools, reasoning, text on
                    stderr), -v. Exit 0 ok, 1 failed or out of turns, 2 bad
                    usage, 3 provider/auth, 4 no such thread, 5 context full,
                    124 timeout, 130 Ctrl-C.
  mcp-serve         Serve agentty's native tools over MCP (stdio). Point any MCP
                    client at `agentty mcp-serve`.
  mcp import        Copy another tool's MCP servers into ~/.agentty/mcp.json (`-
                    from junie|claude|cursor|vscode|codex`, `--dry-run`). No
                    args lists what each tool offers.
  mcp-login <srv>   Authorize an OAuth-gated MCP server from mcp.json (2026-07-
                    28 OAuth 2.1 + PKCE via your browser).
  mcp-logout <srv>  Remove a stored MCP server token.
  mcp-status        List MCP servers and their authorization state.
  diagnostics       Collect a redacted diagnostic bundle for a bug report (build
                    info, logs, config — no secrets)
  skills            List discovered skills with spec-lint diagnostics (exit 1 on
                    warnings — CI-friendly validate)
  config [what]     Every folder agentty reads or writes, where it is and how
                    big. `config <name>` for one, `config env` for the storage
                    variables
  config move       `config move <dir> <path>`: move a folder's data safely,
                    then print the export line to add
  config doctor     Check storage permissions and variables
  config clean      List files old versions left behind (--yes deletes)
  hooks [list]      Show configured lifecycle hooks + approval state
  hooks approve     Inspect + approve the active hooks file (hooks NEVER run
                    unapproved; any change re-gates)
  plugin <verb>     Manage plugins (add | list | remove | approve) — a plugin IS
                    an MCP server, any language, one mcp.json entry: `agentty
                    plugin add today --python today.py`, `--uvx pkg`, `--npx
                    pkg`, `--http <url>`, or `-- cmd args`; add --project for
                    the repo config (approve it with `plugin approve <name> --
                    project`). Docs: /docs/plugins
  rag-bench [dir]   Benchmark search_docs retrieval on your own corpus (recall@k
                    / MRR / nDCG per pipeline stage)
  update            Update agentty to the latest release (--check: only report,
                    don't install)
  version           Print the agentty version and exit
  help              Show this message

options
  -k, --key KEY        API-key override for this session
  -m, --model ID       Model id (e.g. claude-opus-4-5)
  -w, --workspace DIR  Sandbox filesystem tools to this directory (default:
                       cwd). Tools refuse paths outside it. Pass `--workspace /`
                       to disable the gate.
      --sandbox MODE   Wrap bash/diagnostics in an OS-native sandbox (claybin;
                       macOS falls back to sandbox-exec). MODE = auto (default:
                       use if available), on (require backend; fail otherwise),
                       off (disable wrapping).
      --sandbox-backend B
                       Sandbox implementation: claybin (the default and only
                       engine on Linux and Windows; Linux adds seccomp +
                       landlock + cgroup2, macOS uses seatbelt + rlimits). On
                       macOS a host that cannot run claybin falls back to
                       sandbox-exec (one fixed profile), which ignores most
                       Sandbox settings. `bwrap` is accepted and runs claybin.
      --log-file PATH  Write the diagnostic log here instead of
                       ~/.agentty/logs/agentty.log (or $AGENTTY_LOGS_DIR, to
                       move just the logs off the config disk). What gets
                       captured is AGENTTY_LOG (default: warnings and errors) —
                       e.g. AGENTTY_LOG=debug, or AGENTTY_LOG=wire=trace for raw
                       HTTP bytes.
      --events jsonl   Headless `run`: one JSON object per line on stderr:
                       `turn` at each model turn, `reasoning` and `text` as the
                       model writes them, `tool` per tool call (tool, ms, ok,
                       err, args_sha). stdout keeps the answer, so both can be
                       captured.
  -p, --profile MODE   ACP permission tier (Zed shows the prompts): ask
                       (default: prompt write/exec/net), minimal (also prompt
                       reads), write (never prompt reads).
      --provider P     LLM backend. anthropic (default, OAuth/Pro/Max) or an
                       OpenAI-compatible one: openai | codex | groq | openrouter
                       | together | cerebras | deepseek | xai | mistral | gemini
                       | fireworks | ollama | llama.cpp, or a raw host[:port]
                       for any other OpenAI-compatible server. Reads
                       OPENAI_API_KEY (or the provider-specific *_API_KEY) / -k
                       for the key; local backends need no key. Persisted like -
                       m. (Switch live in-app with Ctrl-P — the picker has a
                       "Custom host…" entry too.) chatgpt talks to ChatGPT
                       natively via the reverse-engineered OAuth login (`agentty
                       login` → ChatGPT); no Codex binary is needed. copilot and
                       kimi sign in the same way via their device-flow OAuth
                       (`agentty login` → GitHub Copilot / Kimi) — no API key
                       needed. Note: hosted Claude output is watermarked per the
                       EU AI Act (invisible, no opt-out, set server-side).
                       Local/open-weight backends (ollama, llama.cpp) carry no
                       provider watermark.
  -V, --version        Print the agentty version and exit.
      --auth-header N  Auth header NAME for OpenAI-compatible backends whose
                       gateway doesn't accept `Authorization: Bearer` (e.g. X-
                       API-Key). The key (-k / OPENAI_API_KEY) is sent raw under
                       that name. Session-scoped like -k; default: Bearer.
  -h, --help           Show this message.
outputs.agentty airgap --help:
usage: agentty airgap [--setup] [--clipboard-relay] [--remote-agentty PATH] <user@host>
       agentty airgap [--setup] <user@host> --acp [acp flags…]

  Opens an SSH session to <user@host> with `-R 1080`, which makes
  OpenSSH expose a SOCKS5 proxy on the remote's localhost:1080.
  Connections to it are tunnelled back through SSH and dialed by
  this laptop, so the remote agentty — pointed at the proxy via
  AGENTTY_SOCKS_PROXY — can reach every destination it needs (chat,
  OAuth refresh, web tools) over a single tunnel.  TLS / cert
  verification stay pinned on the real upstream end-to-end, so
  the network path between laptop and remote can't MITM you.

  Trust boundary (read this before --setup): the remote ends up
  with a copy of ~/.agentty/credentials/credentials.json, which contains
  your OAuth refresh token (or API key). A compromised remote
  can therefore exfiltrate your Anthropic credentials independent
  of the tunnel. agentty airgap protects the *network* between
  laptop and remote, not the remote itself — treat the remote as
  a credential-bearing peer, not a sandboxed proxy.

  --setup            Copy ~/.agentty/credentials/credentials.json from
                     this laptop to the remote (chmod 600) before
                     launching.  Run this once on first connect or
                     after re-OAuthing locally.
  --remote-agentty PATH Absolute path to agentty on the remote.  Default:
                     `agentty` (resolved via remote PATH).
  --acp [acp flags…] Don't launch the TUI — instead print a ready-to-
                     paste Zed `agent_servers` config that runs the
                     remote `agentty acp` over this same SSH+SOCKS
                     tunnel, with Zed owning the process. Everything
                     after --acp is forwarded to the remote acp agent
                     (e.g. --acp -m claude-haiku-4-5 --profile ask).
                     Must come AFTER <user@host>.
  --clipboard-relay  Make Ctrl+V paste images and files on the remote.
                     Starts the clipboard agent here and forwards a
                     socket to it, so the remote reads THIS machine's
                     clipboard. Not needed if you ran `agentty paste
                     setup` here: then every ssh session carries it.

  ssh and scp must be on this laptop's PATH.  Pass extra ssh args
  via the AGENTTY_AIRGAP_SSH env var (e.g. -i, -p, -J).

  Without a relay, paste still works for text, and for images in
  terminals that share the clipboard (kitty). `agentty paste doctor`
  on the remote shows which route a paste takes.
outputs.agentty paste help:
agentty paste · images, files and text into agentty, even over ssh and tmux

In the composer, Ctrl+V does all of this for you. These commands set it up and
show what it sees.

on the machine you type on
  setup                   add the ssh hook to ~/.ssh/config and start the agent
                          (once)
  agent                   run the clipboard agent in the foreground

anywhere
  doctor                  show which routes paste would use, and try one
  paste [-o DIR]          print the clipboard: text as is, images and files
                          saved, their paths printed
  config                  list and set the paste settings (Settings → Paste)

when nothing reaches your clipboard (Terminal.app over ssh)
  howto                   one-time Mac or Windows setup to paste images as text
  page > paste.html       a web page that turns a pasted image into one line of
                          text
  encode FILE             FILE as one line of text; paste it anywhere
  decode [DIR]            turn such text on stdin back into files

Pasting an image as text also works in the browser, nothing to install:
agentty.org/paste
